To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed HLA class I/II/TCR triple-knockout T-cells by simultaneous knockout of B2M, CITA, and TRA, which can be used as off-the-shelf T-cells in adoptive immunotherapy.
HLA class I/II/TCR triple-knockout T-cell grafts can evade allogeneicspecific T-cell responses and are suitable for adoptive T-cell therapy.
genetic ablation of HLA class II molecules, HLA class I molecules, and the T cell receptor enables allogeneic-derived T cells to be safely used for adoptive cancer therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of HLA class II and TCR triple-knockout T cell grafts for off-the-shelve adoptive immunotherapy of cancer.
the generation of allogeneically derived T cells that have undergone HLA class I knockout and TCR knockout.
the generation of allogeneically derived antitumor T cells for off-the-shelve adoptive immunotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of the simultaneous knockout of the genes for HLA class I and II and TCR, resulting in allogeneic CAR-T cells that can be safely used in adoptive immunotherapy.
the HLA class I knockout, HLA class I and II knockout, and HLA class I II and TCR knockout T cell lines are all effective and safe in the treatment of cancer.
the use of HLA class II-deficient T cells for off-the-shelve adoptive T cell transfer is feasible and can be used as the universal T cell source for adoptive T cell therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel approach to generate HLA class I-, HLA class II-, and T-cell receptor triple-knockout T-cell grafts that can be used as an off-the-shelf T-cell source for allogeneic adoptive T-cell therapy.
we have developed an allogeneic adoptive T-cell therapy that is safe and efficacious in a mouse tumor model.
we have generated universal antitumor T cells that are devoid of allogene responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HLA class I and HLA class II and TCR triple knockout (tKO) cells are resistant to allogeneic responses, which enables the generation of allogeneically sourced antitumor T cells for adoptive immunotherapy.
HLA class I and HLA class II double-knockout (dKO) T cells can persist better than HLA class I single-knockout (sKO) T cells when cocultured with allogeneics.
the simultaneous ablation of HLA class II and class I, and the TCR, enables the use of allogeneically sourced T cells in adoptive cancer immunotherapies.
